purpose: The predefined rubric a blind reviewer answers over preserved screenshots. It exists so 'the design got better' can be a claim with a method behind it instead of an adjective. It grades what is VISIBLE in the capture; functional acceptance is a separate, independent check and this rubric never restates it.
rules: The reviewer is not the model that produced the screen, and is blind to the request that produced it: it sees the rubric and the captures, nothing else.
Every criterion is answered pass, fail or unclear, with one line quoting what in the capture settles it. 'unclear' is a real answer and is expected whenever the capture cannot show the criterion.
There is no score. No number, no grade, no weighting, no total. A rubric answer is evidence a person reads, not a measurement.

A review is recorded on a criterion whose method is 'review', which the acceptance semantics derive as needs_review and never as satisfied. A second model supplements a person's judgement; it cannot certify in their place.

criteria.name: Hierarchy
criteria.asks: Does one element clearly dominate, and does the eye have an obvious first, second and third stop?
criteria.fail_when: Several elements compete at the same visual weight, or the most important thing on the screen is not the most prominent.
criteria.unclear_when: The capture shows only a fragment of the screen.

criteria.name: Spacing rhythm
criteria.asks: Do the gaps come from one repeating scale, and does whitespace group related things and separate unrelated ones?
criteria.fail_when: Gaps look arbitrary, related items are further apart than unrelated ones, or content is crammed against an edge.

criteria.name: Type scale
criteria.asks: Is there a real, small set of type sizes and weights doing distinct jobs — one display size, quiet body, distinct labels?
criteria.fail_when: Many near-identical sizes, body text at heading weight, or a wall of one size.

criteria.name: Contrast
criteria.asks: Is every piece of text legible against what is behind it, including secondary text, placeholders and text over images?
criteria.fail_when: Any text is hard to read in the capture, or a state is signalled by a hue difference alone.

criteria.name: Responsive integrity
criteria.asks: Comparing the wide and narrow captures: does the layout genuinely reflow, with nothing clipped, overlapping or scrolling sideways?
criteria.fail_when: The narrow capture shows horizontal overflow, overlapping elements, or a desktop layout merely shrunk.

criteria.name: State clarity
criteria.asks: Where a state is captured — loading, empty, error — does it say what happened and what to do next?
criteria.fail_when: A state renders as a blank area, a raw error string, or a spinner with no context.
criteria.unclear_when: No state other than the populated one was captured.

criteria.name: Focus visibility
criteria.asks: In the keyboard-focus capture, is the focused control unmistakable without hunting for it?
criteria.fail_when: No visible focus indicator, or one that disappears against its background.
criteria.unclear_when: No capture shows a focused control.

criteria.name: Consistency with the supplied reference
criteria.asks: Against the supplied reference or the product's existing screens, does this look like the same product — same type, spacing, palette, component shapes?
criteria.fail_when: It reads as a different product, or reinvents a component the reference already has.
